warnings: Frame rate is 30.0 fps (~76.7 deg bowling-arm sweep per frame); release-instant kinematics carry elevated temporal quantization error. Record at 120-240 fps slow-motion outdoors for precision analysis.

calibration_notes: Gravity axis: gravity from 11 standing upright background pose frames.
Panning camera detected: calibrated +X delivery axis from in-frame anatomical stride (spread=0.96 m).

runup_speed_mps.label: Run-Up Approach Speed
runup_speed_mps.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera panning cancels ground-referenced translation without MCC Law 7 pitch calibration; record from a static tripod or supply pitch crease landmarks.
runup_speed_mps.empirical_reference: Elite male fast bowlers: ~5.2–6.6 m/s (strong positive predictor of ball speed)
runup_speed_mps.literature_source: Worthington, King, & Ranson (2013), J. Applied Biomechanics

stride_length_pct_stature.label: Delivery Stride Length
stride_length_pct_stature.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera panning cancels ground-referenced translation without MCC Law 7 pitch calibration; record from a static tripod or supply pitch crease landmarks.
stride_length_pct_stature.empirical_reference: Typical fast bowling stride: ~72–88% of stature (1.30–1.65 m)
stride_length_pct_stature.literature_source: Portus et al. (2004); Worthington et al. (2013)

front_knee_ffc_deg.label: Front Knee Angle at FFC
front_knee_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
front_knee_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Typical FFC contact angle: ~150–170 deg (180 deg = fully straight)

front_knee_br_deg.label: Front Knee Angle at Ball Release
front_knee_br_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
front_knee_br_deg.empirical_reference: Faster bowlers maintain straighter braced front knee (~158–178 deg at BR)
front_knee_br_deg.literature_source: Worthington, King, & Ranson (2013), J. Applied Biomechanics

front_knee_change_deg.label: Front Knee Bracing Change (FFC->BR)
front_knee_change_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
front_knee_change_deg.empirical_reference: Positive (+) = extender/bracer; near 0 = braced; <=-10 deg = flexing/collapsing

trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.label: Upper-Trunk Forward Flexion at FFC
trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
trunk_flexion_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Typical FFC upright/slight-forward posture: ~5–20 deg forward of vertical

trunk_flexion_br_deg.label: Upper-Trunk Forward Flexion at BR
trunk_flexion_br_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
trunk_flexion_br_deg.empirical_reference: Typical elite release trunk flexion: ~35–55 deg forward of vertical

trunk_flexion_delta_deg.label: Trunk Forward Flexion Range (FFC->BR)
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.empirical_reference: Greater forward trunk flexion FFC->BR (~25–42 deg) drives higher ball speed
trunk_flexion_delta_deg.literature_source: Worthington, King, & Ranson (2013), J. Applied Biomechanics

thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg.label: Thorax Contralateral Lateral Flexion at FFC
thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Moderate pre-release side-flexion (~12–28 deg); excessive early bend elevates load
thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg.literature_source: Alway et al. (2021), MSSE; Bayne et al. (2016), JSMS

thorax_lat_flex_br_deg.label: Thorax Contralateral Lateral Flexion at BR
thorax_lat_flex_br_deg.empirical_reference: Uninjured elite norm: ~32–44 deg (40+-8 deg); elevated LBSI risk around >=48–50 deg

pelvis_alignment_bfc_deg.label: Pelvis Alignment at BFC
pelvis_alignment_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: AIS convention: <=205 deg side-on, 205–245 deg semi, >245 deg front-on

shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.label: Shoulder Alignment at BFC
shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: total 1-sigma uncertainty (+-14.9 deg) exceeds scientific reliability limit (14.0 deg) due to view/FPS/blur constraints.
shoulder_alignment_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: AIS convention: <=205 deg side-on, 205–245 deg semi, >245 deg front-on

shoulder_counter_rotation_deg.label: Shoulder Counter-Rotation (SCR, BFC->FFC)
shoulder_counter_rotation_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: total 1-sigma uncertainty (+-15.6 deg) exceeds scientific reliability limit (13.5 deg) due to view/FPS/blur constraints.
shoulder_counter_rotation_deg.empirical_reference: <25-30 deg = non-mixed alignment; >=30 deg defines mixed action linked to LBSI

hip_shoulder_sep_bfc_deg.label: Hip-Shoulder Separation at BFC
hip_shoulder_sep_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: BFC misalignment >=30 deg with counter-rotation indicates mixed action loading

max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.label: Peak Dynamic Hip-Shoulder Separation
max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.empirical_reference: Well-timed late separation (~25–50 deg) supports stretch-shortening momentum transfer
max_hip_shoulder_sep_deg.literature_source: Portus et al. (2004); Worthington et al. (2013)

delayed_arm_ffc_deg.label: Delayed Bowling Arm Angle Behind Vertical at FFC
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: 30.0 fps causes ~77 deg bowling-arm sweep per frame; high-velocity arm kinematics require >=100 fps (ideally 120-240 fps).
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Larger delay behind vertical (~125–165 deg at FFC) strongly predicts higher ball speed
delayed_arm_ffc_deg.literature_source: Worthington, King, & Ranson (2013), J. Applied Biomechanics

rear_hip_bfc_deg.label: Rear Hip Angle at BFC
rear_hip_bfc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
rear_hip_bfc_deg.empirical_reference: Key upstream lumbopelvic control predictor in prospective LBSI regression model
rear_hip_bfc_deg.literature_source: Alway, Felton, Brooke-Wavell, Peirce, & King (2021), MSSE

pelvic_drop_ffc_deg.label: Contralateral/Ipsilateral Pelvic Tilt at FFC
pelvic_drop_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: Controlled level pelvis (|tilt| <10 deg) reduces asymmetrical lumbar shear loading

non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.label: Non-Bowling (Front) Arm Elevation at FFC
non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.suppression_reason: Suppressed: camera azimuth (-3 deg, view=rear_behind_bowler) cannot reliably resolve sagittal (side-on) kinematics; film from a side-on (~90 deg) angle.
non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.empirical_reference: High front-arm anchor (>15 deg above horizontal at FFC) supports trunk alignment before pull
non_bowling_arm_elev_ffc_deg.literature_source: Middleton et al.; Worthington et al.

peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.label: Peak Bowling Arm Angular Velocity
peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.suppression_reason: Suppressed: 30.0 fps causes ~77 deg bowling-arm sweep per frame; high-velocity arm kinematics require >=100 fps (ideally 120-240 fps).
peak_arm_angular_vel_dps.empirical_reference: Elite fast bowlers peak ~2,000–2,570 deg/s (35–45 rad/s) near ball release

release_height_m.label: Ball Release Height
release_height_m.empirical_reference: Typically ~1.05–1.18x bowler stature (~1.95–2.20 m for 1.85 m bowler)

follow_through_drift_deg.label: Follow-Through Lateral Drift Angle
follow_through_drift_deg.empirical_reference: Driving momentum near target line (|drift| <12-15 deg) reduces lateral braking shear

icc_elbow_legality_verdict.label: ICC 15-Degree Elbow Legality Verdict
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.suppression_reason: Permanently refused: even dual-camera markerless OpenCap exhibits 22.7 deg RMSE on cricket elbow flexion (Abraham et al., 2025/2026), exceeding the entire 15-degree ICC threshold. Authoritative legality testing requires an ICC-accredited >=250 Hz 3D optical lab.
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.empirical_reference: ICC limit: <=15 deg active elbow extension strictly between UAH and BR
icc_elbow_legality_verdict.literature_source: Elliott, Alderson, & Denver (2007); Abraham, Feros, & Fox (2025/2026)

kinetic_efficiency.name: Kinetic & Pace Efficiency
kinetic_efficiency.summary: Too few primary pace-efficiency kinematics (front-knee bracing, trunk flexion, delayed arm, run-up speed) were reliably observable from this camera view and frame rate.

lumbar_load_screening.name: Mechanical Load & Durability Screening
lumbar_load_screening.summary: Durability index 89.7 +- 14.0 / 100 (Low Mechanical Load Flag) from 4 observable lumbar-loading markers (thorax_lat_flex_br_deg, thorax_lat_flex_ffc_deg, pelvic_drop_ffc_deg, follow_through_drift_deg).

quadrant.interpretation: Full 2D Performance-Durability placement requires both sagittal (side-on) kinetic evidence and coronal/transverse (rear or 45-deg) spinal-load evidence.

strengths.title: Controlled Contralateral Trunk Clearance
strengths.biomechanical_mechanism: Thorax lateral flexion at release (30.2 deg) sits cleanly within the uninjured elite fast-bowling reference range (Bayne et al., 2016: 40 +- 8 deg).
strengths.actionable_recommendation: Maintain current lateral trunk stability as bowling intensity increases.

capture_upgrades.title: Switch Smartphone to 120–240 fps Slow-Motion
capture_upgrades.biomechanical_mechanism: Current clip is 30.0 fps (~77 deg arm sweep per frame), creating severe temporal aliasing near release.
capture_upgrades.actionable_recommendation: Record outdoors in native 1080p 240 fps slow-motion to reduce timing uncertainty by up to 8x.

capture_upgrades.title: Use a Static Tripod Showing Pitch Creases
capture_upgrades.biomechanical_mechanism: Camera panning hides ground-referenced run-up velocity and true BFC-to-FFC stride displacement.
capture_upgrades.actionable_recommendation: Mount the camera on a stationary tripod framing both popping/bowling creases and the bowler's full body.

capture_upgrades.title: Add a Side-On (90 deg) Camera Angle
capture_upgrades.biomechanical_mechanism: Rear/front cameras cannot accurately resolve sagittal front-knee bracing or forward trunk flexion.
capture_upgrades.actionable_recommendation: Place a tripod phone 8-12 m perpendicular to the popping crease showing the full run-up to follow-through.

hard_guardrails: ICC 15-degree elbow legality CANNOT be adjudicated from monocular or casual 2D/3D video; accredited >=250 Hz 3D optical lab testing is required.
Mechanical load screening estimates stress per delivery only and is NOT a medical diagnosis; actual injury risk depends strongly on bowling workload, age/skeletal maturity, and physical capacity.
